title: cli/storage: let the console frame a PDF from the storage origin, and document the bucket CORS the file preview needs
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Development card for decision #34781, option A, ruled by the maintainer on {{WAS:2026-11-22T12:07Z}}. This is the server and CLI half of the in-page file preview. Filed by the seat. Parent: #34781.

## What happens

- The console's Content-Security-Policy has no `frame-src` (`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`, around lines 919 to 934). On a deployment whose files are served from an S3-compatible bucket on another origin, an embedded PDF preview is blocked.
- Text and CSV previews read the file from object storage in the browser, which needs the bucket's CORS to allow the console origin.

## To do

1. Add the configured storage origin to `frame-src`, and nothing wider. With local storage, the console's own origin is enough.
2. Document the bucket CORS rule the preview needs, in the storage deployment docs.
3. When the bucket does not allow the read, the preview falls back to opening the file in a new tab. That fallback lives in the ui card; this card states the contract it relies on.

## Acceptance

- On an S3-backed deployment, a PDF preview loads in the dialog, and the CSP names only the storage origin as an extra frame source.
- The storage docs state the CORS rule, and a deployment without it still lets the user open the file in a new tab.

## Grade
p2 · area:ux · domain:server. Small. Needed by the ui card on S3 deployments.
